title: Tens and ones

parent.why: Bundling 10 sticks with a rubber band makes big piles easy to count: count the bundles in tens, then the loose sticks.
The left digit counts tens, the right digit counts ones. This is why 34 and 43 are different numbers.
1+9, 2+8, 3+7, 4+6, 5+5. Knowing them by heart makes adding past 10 easy (see Adding).
25 and 10 more: the tens digit goes up by one, the ones stay — 35.

ask: Bundle 10 straws or sticks with a rubber band. Make 2 bundles and 3 loose ones: how many?
How many fingers do 2 people have? Count in tens.
Write the number with 5 tens and 2 ones.

rounds.h: 7 and 3 more makes ten. Count on from 7: 8, 9, 10 — that's 3.
5 and 5 — one full hand each — make ten.

rounds.t: How many fingers on two hands?
One bundle has 10 sticks. How many sticks in 2 bundles?

rounds.h: 1 ten is 10, and 4 ones more is 14.
3 tens is 30, and 5 ones more is 35.
16 − 10 = 6, so 6 ones are left after the ten.
The left digit counts tens, so the 6 is 6 tens (60).

rounds.t: Which number has 8 tens and 1 one?
rounds.h: 8 tens is 80, plus 1 is 81. 18 is 1 ten and 8 ones.
10 more adds one ten: 2 tens become 3 tens, the 5 ones stay — 35.
9 ones + 1 makes a new ten, and 9 tens + 1 ten makes ten tens: 100.
